headline: AI models predict drug responses from single-cell, transcriptomic, and imaging data
label: Ai Drug Response Modeling
summary: Recent papers pair AI with single-cell, transcriptomic, and network data to predict and prioritize drug responses and combinations.
synthesis: The dominant thread is computational prioritization of therapeutic interventions, including target pairs, drug combinations, and repurposable compounds, built on single-cell, transcriptomic, imaging, or knowledge-graph data. Emet, an AI agent over a 1.5B-triple biomedical knowledge graph, proposed lung squamous cell carcinoma target pairs, with CDC7+PKMYT1 showing synergy in two cell lines. PHAROS couples a pretrained single-cell perturbation model to a search over drug combinations, while MNRS prioritizes combinations from longitudinal blood transcriptomics. Other items apply neural networks to ARCHS4 transcriptomes, random forests to single-cell Raman spectra for melanoma resistance, and high-content imaging to AML subtype drug responses. Reviews position AI virtual cells and digital twins as predictive models of unmeasured responses. Not every item carries experimental validation; several are computational pipelines. What is new is the pairing of predictive modeling with cell-level testing across these data types.
